parsed.explanation: The combined regime shows no criminalisation of trans identity or same-sex conduct, a constitutional and statutory ban on gender-identity discrimination with criminal penalties and sentencing aggravation, and a straightforward 2016 legal-recognition procedure. No traveller-facing exposure is documented: no border document friction, facility bans, custody placement rules, police targeting, or care denial for visitors. Offsetting this, enforcement is documented as weak (2017 ombudsman: LGBT murders largely unsolved, no sentences), a 2024 survey records widespread LGBTI exclusion, and societal discrimination is common. No remedy is shown operating for a visitor, and no subnational or minor-specific regime exists. Absence of documented visitor incidents plus robust paper protections, discounted by thin enforcement, places this in Reduced Risk's upper half.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border, visa, marker-mismatch, or screening friction appears in the record.
entry_documents.protection: Constitutional non-discrimination on gender identity (2009) and the 2010 anti-discrimination law apply to services and public spheres, extending a general protective backdrop at entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home documents are never questioned in the record; recognition procedure is resident-facing only.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented for visitors. Enforcement failure (few LGBT murder investigations, no convictions, 2017) concerns impunity for violence against locals, not detention of trans travellers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Gender-identity motive is a statutory aggravating circumstance (art. 40bis, 2010); gender-identity discrimination carries 1–5 years' imprisonment.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Weak enforcement blunts these protections, but no custody pathway for a trans visitor is recorded.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access restriction, ward placement rule, or birth-sex segregation appears.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Constitutional guarantee of bodily integrity and equal exercise of rights.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational variation documented; record explicitly finds none.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No emergency-care denial, medication seizure, or marker-based refusal for visitors appears.
care_services.protection: 2010 law bars gender-identity discrimination in health; blood-donation ban lifted (2019) is a climate signal.
care_services.interaction: Resident recognition procedure does not touch visitor care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented societal discrimination is common; 2024 survey records widespread LGBTI exclusion — but this is a broad, not trans- or traveller-specific figure, and frames exclusion, not threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Transphobia defined and criminalised (2010); incitement punishable; military service open to trans people since 2015.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Street-level disapproval is friction/hostility at most; no state threat-framing recorded.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No minor-specific or guardian-specific restriction appears.
minors_guardians.protection: Adoption open to single people regardless of orientation; children's code art. 84 covers free unions — resident-facing climate signals only.
minors_guardians.interaction: Nothing in the record shows a family visit or accompanied minor triggering exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: LGBT murders documented as rarely investigated with zero sentences (2017 ombudsman) — impunity signal, but no rate, no trans-specific count, no background comparison, and dated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity motive aggravates sentencing; discrimination and incitement criminalised.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Impunity weakens recourse if a visitor were assaulted; no documented pattern of targeted sweeps or police hostility.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement shown weak in the only data year (2017); no recent figures; societal discrimination reports common.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional complaint routes, ombudsman, anti-discrimination law, criminal penalties, and a confidential 15-day recognition process exist on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protections are not shown operating or failing for visitors specifically — an open question, not an exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.65-B involves a visitor actually refused care and misgendered, with remedies that worked. This dossier documents no visitor-facing incident on any axis; its negatives are enforcement gaps and broad societal exclusion. Higher than 0.65-B because no concrete traveller exposure exists here, lower than 0.85 because remedies are not shown operating.

0.75-C has documented brief border detention with functioning tribunal remedies and officer discretion. This dossier has no documented border friction at all, but also no shown remedy working — weaker enforcement of a comparably strong protective framework. Similar tier: low-moderate severity, uncertainty about real-world application.

0.85-A pairs explicit equality coverage with documented prompt remedies (apologies, compensation) against isolated friction. This dossier matches the legal architecture but lacks evidence of remedies functioning and adds documented widespread discrimination and murder impunity, so it sits below this anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines strong traveller-neutral protections (constitutional and statutory gender-identity non-discrimination, criminal penalties, an aggravating-circumstance provision, no criminalisation since 1832) with zero documented visitor-facing restrictions on entry, documents, facilities, custody, or care. The chief weaknesses are enforcement, not law: the only data year (2017) shows LGBT murders going unsentenced, and a 2024 survey records broad LGBTI exclusion — both local-sphere and only partly trans-specific. Marriage exclusion for a relationship read as same-sex is resident-facing; free union supplies an alternative. No subnational regime, minor-specific rule, or police-targeting pattern exists in the record. The absence of documented exposure against a robust but weakly enforced framework supports a Reduced-Risk rating in its upper half, with enforcement performance the main open question.
